# grok CLI help captured 2026-10-31 from npm @xai-official/grok@1.0.70 (dist-tag latest; alpha=1.0.73). No login; isolated HOME. GROUND TRUTH for flags.

===== grok help
Grok Build TUI

Usage: grok [OPTIONS] [PROMPT] [COMMAND]

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]
          Initial prompt for the interactive session.
          
          For example, `grok "fix the bug"` or `grok --worktree=feat "create this feature"`.

Options:
      --add-dir <DIR>
          Also work in this folder, beside the working directory (repeatable).
          
          A relative path starts from the working directory. A resumed session keeps the folders it was created with. Refused if the folder isn't trusted or the agent works only in its working directory.

      --agent <NAME>
          Agent name or definition file path

      --agents <JSON>
          Inline subagent definitions as JSON

      --allow <RULE>
          Permission allow rule (compat aliases: --allowedTools, --allowed-tools)

      --always-approve
          Auto-approve all tool executions

  -c, --continue
          Continue the most recent session for the current working directory

      --cwd <CWD>
          Working directory

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

      --deny <RULE>
          Permission deny rule (compat alias: --disallowedTools)

      --disable-web-search
          Disable web search and web fetch tools

      --disallowed-tools <TOOLS>
          Built-in tools to remove (comma-separated)

      --fork-session
          When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original.
          
          Applies to `--resume` / `--continue`. `--session-id` can set the new ID.

      --fullscreen
          Open in the standard fullscreen TUI for this session.
          
          Overrides a config `[ui] screen_mode = "minimal"` preference. Session-scoped only, does not write config. Fullscreen-vs-inline still follows the alt-screen policy (--no-alt-screen, [terminal] alt_screen, terminal auto-detection).

  -h, --help
          Print help (see more with 'grok help')

      --include-partial-messages
          Emit incremental text and thinking deltas alongside whole messages.
          
          The deltas are `stream_event` lines. Only affects `--output-format streaming-messages-json`.

      --json-schema <SCHEMA>
          JSON Schema for structured output.
          
          When set, the model is constrained to produce JSON matching this schema. Implies --output-format json. Example: --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}}}'

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`

  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model ID to use

      --max-turns <N>
          Maximum number of agent turns

      --minimal
          Experimental: scrollback-native rendering.
          
          Finalized blocks are printed into the terminal's native scrollback (use the terminal's own scroll / selection). Session-scoped only, does not write config.

      --no-alt-screen
          Run inline instead of using the terminal alternate screen

      --no-plan
          Disable plan mode

      --no-subagents
          Disable subagent spawning

      --oauth
          Force browser (loopback) login when the welcome screen authenticates

      --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>
          Output format for headless mode

          Possible values:
          - plain
          - json
          - streaming-json:          NDJSON: one ACP session update per line, the agent's native format
          - streaming-messages-json: NDJSON in the Anthropic Messages API wire format
          
          [default: plain]

  -p, --single <PROMPT>
          Single-turn prompt. Prints the response to stdout and exits

      --permission-mode <MODE>
          Permission mode
          
          [possible values: default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan]

      --prompt-file <PATH>
          Single-turn prompt from a file

      --prompt-json <JSON>
          Single-turn prompt as JSON content blocks

  -r, --resume [<SESSION_ID_OR_TITLE>]
          Resume a session by ID or title, or the most recent if omitted.
          
          Non-ID values match session titles for the current directory, ignoring letter case; UUID-shaped values always mean IDs. Without an exact match, the same words joined by any separators also match: quote "fix login bug" or write fix-login-bug. Among duplicate titles a sole renamed match wins; otherwise the resume fails as ambiguous.

      --reasoning-effort <EFFORT>
          Reasoning effort for reasoning models
          
          [aliases: --effort]

      --restore-code
          Restore the original session's repository snapshot when resuming.
          
          Remote sessions require `--worktree` (never checks out into the current directory). Without this flag, resume restores conversation only.

      --rules <RULES>
          Extra rules to append to the system prompt

  -s, --session-id <SESSION_ID>
          Use a specific session UUID for a new conversation.
          
          For a **new** conversation the id must be a valid UUID and must not already exist under the target session directory. With `--resume`/`--continue`, only valid together with `--fork-session` (names the forked session). Does not resume existing sessions, use `--resume` / `--continue` instead.

      --sandbox <PROFILE>
          Sandbox profile for filesystem and network access
          
          [env: GROK_SANDBOX=]

      --system-prompt-override <PROMPT>
          Override the agent's system prompt (compat alias: --system-prompt)

      --tools <TOOLS>
          Built-in tools to allow (comma-separated)

  -v, --version
          Print version

      --verbatim
          Send the prompt exactly as given

  -w, --worktree [<WORKTREE>]
          Start the session in a new git worktree, optionally named.
          
          With `--resume` of a remote session, pass `--restore-code` to apply the snapshot codebase (conversation is restored either way).

      --worktree-ref <WORKTREE_REF>
          Branch, tag, or commit to base the worktree on (with `--worktree`).
          
          Defaults to the current HEAD of the source checkout when omitted.
          
          [aliases: --ref]

Commands:
  agent        Run Grok without the interactive UI
  clone        Lazy-clone a git repository via grove (NFS on macOS, FUSE on Linux)
  completions  Generate shell completion scripts (bash, zsh, fish, powershell, ...)
  dashboard    Open the Agent Dashboard view at startup
  doctor       Check terminal, clipboard, color, and input support without starting Grok
  du           Show what the grok home (~/.grok) uses on disk [aliases: disk-usage]
  export       Export a session transcript as Markdown
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
  inspect      Show the configuration Grok discovers for this directory
  leader       Manage running leader processes
  login        Sign in to Grok
  logout       Sign out and clear cached credentials
  mcp          Manage MCP server configurations
  memory       Manage cross-session memory
  models       List available models and exit
  plugin       Manage plugins and marketplace sources
  sessions     List, search, or restore sessions
  setup        Fetch and install managed configuration
  trace        Export or upload session trace data
  update       Check for updates or install a specific version
  usage        Print persisted token and cost usage for a session
  version      Print version information [aliases: v]
  worker       Run this machine as a Cursor private worker
  worktree     Manage git worktrees
  wrap         Run any command with local clipboard support

===== grok agent --help
Run Grok without the interactive UI

Usage: grok agent [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  stdio     Run the agent over stdio
  headless  Run the agent headlessly over the Grok WebSocket relay
  serve     Run the agent as a WebSocket server
  leader    Run as the shared leader process for other clients
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --reauth
          Run authentication before starting the agent [aliases: ----reauthenticate]
  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model ID to use
      --reasoning-effort <EFFORT>
          Reasoning effort for reasoning models [aliases: --effort]
      --always-approve
          Auto-approve all tool executions
      --agent-profile <PATH>
          Path to an agent profile file
      --plugin-dir <DIR>
          Load a plugin from this directory for this process only (repeatable)
      --leader
          Connect to a shared leader process instead of starting a new agent
      --no-leader
          Start a new agent even when config enables leader mode
      --grok-ws-origin <GROK_WS_ORIGIN>
          
      --grok-ws-url <GROK_WS_URL>
          
      --cli-chat-proxy-base-url <CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL>
          Override the CLI chat proxy base URL
      --xai-api-base-url <XAI_API_BASE_URL>
          Override the public xAI API base URL
      --debug
          Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE
  -h, --help
          Print help (see more with 'grok help agent')
      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. ===== grok worker --help
Run this machine as a Cursor private worker

Usage: grok worker [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start       Run a leader in this terminal until Ctrl+C
  stop        Unregister from Cursor and release the claims (the leader keeps running)
  status      Show the current worker status and its Cloud Agent claims [aliases: list]
  controller  Claim pending Cloud Agent requests for team pools and run a spawn hook for each
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --name <NAME>                     Worker display name shown in Cursor [env: CURSOR_WORKER_NAME=]
      --worker-dir <DIR>                Repository directory offered to Cursor Cloud Agents
      --max-agents <N>                  Maximum concurrent Cloud Agent claims
      --pool [<NAME>]                   Join a team Self-Hosted Pool
      --single-use                      Same as `--pool` (legacy alias)
      --pool-name <NAME>                Deprecated alias for `--pool <NAME>`. Needs `--pool` or `--single-use`
      --mint-github-token               Let Cursor send the pool worker short-lived GitHub tokens during a claimed run
      --sync-dashboard-secrets          Let Cursor send the pool worker the team's dashboard secrets as env variables
      --clone-git-repos                 Clone the claimed run's repository with the minted token
      --label <KEY=VALUE>               Routing label for the worker, as `key=value`. Repeatable
      --labels-file <PATH>              JSON or TOML file of worker labels. Cannot be combined with `--label` [env: CURSOR_WORKER_LABELS_FILE=]
      --api-key <KEY>                   Cursor API key the worker registers with, in place of your linked Cursor account [env: CURSOR_API_KEY]
      --auth-token-file <PATH>          File holding the worker's Cursor auth token, re-read before every reconnect
      --on-session-start <COMMAND>      Command run on this host once a pool claim lands. Needs `--pool`
      --on-session-end <COMMAND>        Command run on this host once a pool claim is released. Needs `--pool`
      --identity-socket                 Give each Cloud Agent its own OIDC identity socket
      --management-addr <ADDRESS>       Serve worker health over HTTP for Kubernetes probes
      --idle-release-timeout <SECONDS>  Seconds a claim may sit idle before Cursor releases it. 0 turns this off [env: CURSOR_WORKER_IDLE_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=]
      --debug                           Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>               Write debug logs to FILE
  -h, --help                            Print help (see more with 'grok help worker')
      --leader-socket <PATH>            Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`

===== grok usage --help
Print persisted token and cost usage for a session

Usage: grok usage [OPTIONS] <SESSION_ID> [TURN]

Arguments:
  <SESSION_ID>
          Session ID

  [TURN]
          Turn number. Omit for session totals and every recorded turn

Options:
      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`

===== grok worktree --help
Manage git worktrees

Usage: grok worktree [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create           Create a worktree the way `grok -w` does, without starting a session
  list             List the registry's worktrees, unfinished copies and Grove clones [aliases: ls]
  show             Show details for a specific worktree
  rm               Remove worktrees, or Grove clones through the daemon that owns them
  gc               Remove expired worktrees, keeping any whose work would not survive
  detach           Convert a Grove-projected worktree into a plain git worktree
  salvage          Recover a Grove worktree's hydrated and dirty files when its source repo is gone
  clean-artifacts  Purge escape-dir artifact contents (`git clean` does not)
  redirect         Inspect and repair artifact-directory redirections
  db               Database maintenance
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --debug                 Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>     Write debug logs to FILE
  -h, --help                  Print help (see more with 'grok help worktree')
      --leader-socket <PATH>  Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`

===== grok worktree create --help
Create a worktree the way `grok -w` does, without starting a session

Usage: grok worktree create [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments:
  [NAME]
          Worktree name; generated when omitted

Options:
      --ref <REF>
          Branch, tag, or commit to base the worktree on.
          
          Without it, HEAD plus uncommitted changes

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`

===== grok sessions --help
List, search, or restore sessions

Usage: grok sessions [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List recent sessions (same as search with no query)
  search  Search sessions by keyword
  delete  Permanently delete a session from history
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --debug                 Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>     Write debug logs to FILE
  -h, --help                  Print help (see more with 'grok help sessions')
      --leader-socket <PATH>  Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`

===== grok plugin --help
Manage plugins and marketplace sources

Usage: grok plugin [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list         List installed plugins
  install      Install a plugin from a git URL or local path
  uninstall    Uninstall an installed plugin by name [aliases: rm, remove]
  update       Update installed plugin(s)
  enable       Enable a disabled plugin
  disable      Disable a plugin without uninstalling it
  details      Show a plugin's component inventory
  validate     Validate a plugin manifest
  tag          Create a release git tag from the plugin's manifest version
  marketplace  Manage marketplace sources
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --debug                 Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>     Write debug logs to FILE
  -h, --help                  Print help (see more with 'grok help plugin')
      --leader-socket <PATH>  Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`

===== grok plugin install --help
Install a plugin from a git URL or local path

Usage: grok plugin install [OPTIONS] <SOURCE>

Arguments:
  <SOURCE>
          Git URL, GitHub shorthand (user/repo), or local path.
          
          Supports @ref suffix (e.g. user/repo@v1.0) and #subdir.

Options:
      --trust
          Trust the plugin immediately (skip confirmation prompt)

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`

===== grok setup --help
Fetch and install managed configuration

Usage: grok setup [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Print the fetched configuration as JSON instead of installing it.
          
          Writes nothing to ~/.grok.

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.

===== grok update --help
Check for updates or install a specific version

Usage: grok update [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --check
          Check for updates without installing

      --json
          Emit machine-readable JSON output (for --check)

      --force-reinstall
          Force re-download and install even if already up to date

      --version <VERSION>
          Install a specific version (e.g. 0.1.150 or 0.1.151-alpha.2)

      --alpha
          Switch to the alpha release channel (faster updates, may have bugs)

      --stable
          Switch to the stable release channel (default, weekly releases)

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`
